title: The finite fibre component has a clopen image in the integral closure
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finite-type map of commutative rings, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and write $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ with $C_1$ finite over $A/I$ (a finitely generated $A/I$-module); let $\varepsilon=(1,0)\in B/IB$, so $C_1=\varepsilon(B/IB)$ and $C_2=(1-\varepsilon)(B/IB)$. Let $B'\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$ (the elements of $B$ that are roots of monic polynomials with coefficients in the image of $A$), let $\phi:\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B')$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak q\cap B'$, be induced by this inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ be the set of inverse images of the primes of $C_1$ under the surjection $B\to B/IB\to C_1$; similarly $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is the set $V(IB')$ of primes containing $IB'$. Suppose $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is open, $T\subseteq\phi^{-1}(U)$, and the induced morphism $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces (a homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms on all section rings and local rings). Then $\phi(T)$ is open and closed in $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')$, its inverse image under $\phi$ is exactly $T$, and the resulting product decomposition $B'/IB'=C'_1\times C'_2$ has $C'_1\to C_1$ an isomorphism and maps $C'_1$ into $C_1$ and $C'_2$ into $C_2$. Precisely: there is a unique idempotent $\varepsilon'\in B'/IB'$ such that $\phi(T)$ is the set of primes of $B'$ containing $IB'$ and not containing a (any) lift of $\varepsilon'$; with $C'_1=\varepsilon'(B'/IB')$ and $C'_2=(1-\varepsilon')(B'/IB')$, the ring map $B'/IB'\to B/IB$ induced by the inclusion sends $\varepsilon'$ to $\varepsilon$, and its restriction $C'_1\to C_1$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex:2529-2541, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH: image of T is open in the closed fibre, finite-over-the-base gives closedness, then clopen-to-product decomposition and factor identification. proof.text: Construct the induced quotient homomorphism f using Ideal.Quotient.lift. Ideal.map_map and the integral-closure scalar tower show map iota IB prime=IB; this proves quotient compatibility.
Invoke the general, fully proved quotient-factor openness theorem with this ideal equality and the isomorphism over U.

Finiteness makes the A/I -> C1 map integral. Composing with the surjection A -> A/I remains integral, and hcompat identifies this composition with A -> B prime -> C1. RingHom.IsIntegral.tower_top implies B prime -> C1 is integral. Its spectrum map is closed, so its range phi(T) is closed. Pull back along the continuous quotient spectrum map and combine with openness.
On phi^{-1}(U), use injectivity of the homeomorphism underlying the scheme isomorphism: if phi(q)=phi(t) with t in T, both lie over U, so q=t. Thus phi^{-1}(phi(T))=T.

Obtain c and its uniqueness from the clopen-idempotent correspondence. Every point of phi(T) belongs to the range of the quotient spectrum map because iota sends IB prime into IB. The quotient map is injective on spectra, so image of D(c) equals phi(T), and uniqueness in this image formulation follows from uniqueness in the inverse-image formulation.

The shared firstFactor_range theorem from QuotientFirstFactorImageOpen identifies the image of Spec(C1) in Spec(B/IB) with D(e^{-1}(1,0)): kernel containment in a prime is equivalent to omitting this idempotent by multiplication and their complementary sum 1. Pulling back the equation for D(c) through f, and using the commutative quotient square and phi^{-1}phi(T)=T, proves D(f(c))=D(e^{-1}(1,0)). Injectivity of basicOpen on idempotents yields f(c)=e^{-1}(1,0).

The image of D(c) equals phi(T) and is contained in U. Apply the general quotient first-factor identification lemma with f, c, the ideal equality, and the restricted isomorphism. This supplies the product decomposition and its compatible first-factor ring isomorphism and second-factor homomorphism.

split_report.summary: Split along the Stacks proof of 09XH (more-algebra.tex:2529-2541): T = V(IB) ∩ D(lift of ε) (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus, Tag 00E5); φ^{-1}(V(IB')) = V(IB); openness of φ(T) in V(IB') via the homeomorphism over U; closedness via finite ⇒ integral and integral ⇒ closed Spec map (Stacks 00GU/00HZ); clopen ⇒ idempotent ε' (00EE/00EM); φ^{-1}φ(T) = T by injectivity over U; ε' ↦ ε by uniqueness of idempotents; C'_1 ≅ C_1 by choosing g lifting ε' with D(g) ⊆ U, B'_g ≅ B_g, and reducing mod IB'+(1−g)B' (Stacks proves C'_1 = C_1 only after choosing g, so the g-construction of choose-g is repeated here: choose-g's statement assumes C'_1 ≅ C_1 and cannot be cited). Statement made precise (ε', C'_i = ε'(B'/IB'), conventions for Spec C_1 ⊆ Spec B); stmt_deps reduced to the notions used (lemma ids removed, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism added). Brief's tag 00EE for disjoint-implies-product corrected: that lemma is 00EM; 00EE is disjoint-decomposition (idempotents).

lean.statement: theorem integralClosure_finiteFibre_image_clopen {A : Type v} {B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] (I : Ideal A) {C₁ : Type w} {C₂ : Type z} [CommRing C₁] [CommRing C₂] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) C₁] [Module.Finite (A ⧸ I) C₁] (e : (B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) I) ≃+* C₁ × C₂) (hcompat : ∀ a : A, algebraMap (A ⧸ I) C₁ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a) = (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A B a))).1) (U : (Spec (.of (integralClosure A B))).Opens) (hiso : IsIso (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (integralClosure A B) B)) ∣_ U)) : let R := B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) I let R' := (integralClosure A B) ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B)) I let π := Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) I) let π' := Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B)) I) let ι := algebraMap (integralClosure A B) B let φ := PrimeSpectrum.comap ι let β := (RingHom.fst C₁ C₂).comp (e.toRingHom.comp π) let T := Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap β) T ⊆ φ ⁻¹' U.1 → ∃ (f : R' →+* R), (∀ b, f (π' b) = π (ι b)) ∧ IsClopen ((PrimeSpectrum.comap π') ⁻¹' (φ '' T)) ∧ φ ⁻¹' (φ '' T) = T ∧ ∃ (ε' : R'), IsIdempotentElem ε' ∧ φ '' T = PrimeSpectrum.comap π' '' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen ε' : Set _) ∧ (∀ δ : R', IsIdempotentElem δ → φ '' T = PrimeSpectrum.comap π' '' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen δ : Set _) → δ = ε') ∧ f ε' = e.symm (1, 0) ∧ ∃ (C'₁ C'₂ : Type u) (_ : CommRing C'₁) (_ : CommRing C'₂) (e' : R' ≃+* C'₁ × C'₂) (g : C'₁ ≃+* C₁) (h : C'₂ →+* C₂), e' ε' = (1, 0) ∧ ∀ r : R', e (f r) = (g (e' r).1, h (e' r).2)
